question: Should outbound message actions treat object-shaped JSON `channelData` as sufficient send content across message-tool and internal-source-reply paths, with whole-payload suppression whenever protected runtime context is detected?
rationale: This is a durable core boundary for opaque channel/plugin payloads: the patch is internally consistent, but source inspection cannot determine whether the intended product contract is universal acceptance, a narrower channel allowlist, or a different sanitization policy.

options.title: Confirm the shared opaque-payload contract
options.body: Accept parsed object-shaped `channelData` as send content and retain the PR's fail-closed whole-payload suppression rule after the final merge/check refresh.

options.title: Narrow the accepted payload boundary
options.body: Require a channel/plugin-specific contract or allowlist before `channelData` can satisfy send-content validation, then adjust the shared helper and tests.

options.title: Keep current validation semantics
options.body: Reject payload-only `channelData` sends and close the change if the compatibility gain does not justify broadening the opaque-content boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm the shared opaque-payload contract
recommendation.body: Accept parsed object-shaped `channelData` as send content and retain the PR's fail-closed whole-payload suppression rule after the final merge/check refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work owns source-reply routing and message-tool structured delivery behavior.
